code_label: Computational burden of pricing and risk
text_span: the fair valuation of financial derivatives, known as pricing, and the computation of various risk measures, such as the Value at Risk (VaR), have become two of the tasks that consume a great amount of computational resources
rationale: States the motivating problem and why it matters computationally.

code_label: Monte Carlo as de facto standard
text_span: Monte Carlo-simulation (MC) techniques or numerical algorithms for solving partial differential equations (PDE). The key advantage of MC technique is that it is easy to implement, very general and scales well with the dimension of the problem.
rationale: Summarizes the classical baseline methods and their appeal.

code_label: Quadratic speedup promise of QAMC
text_span: This technique promises to be as flexible and general as its classical counterpart while requiring quadratically fewer computational steps.
rationale: Captures the central claimed advantage of quantum accelerated Monte Carlo.

code_label: PDE methods may offer exponential speedups
text_span: some methods that promise to obtain even exponential speedups. However, such speedups can only be attained for very specific cases
rationale: States both the promise and the restriction of PDE-based quantum methods.

code_label: NISQ focus due to hardware limits
text_span: limitations in the number of qubits, in the depth of the circuits and in the levels of “noise”. Hence, the current deliverable pays special focus to quantum algorithms in Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) computers.
rationale: Explains the hardware constraints shaping the review.

code_label: Review scope since prior deliverable
text_span: This document reviews several techniques for derivatives pricing and the computation of VaR that have been introduced in the literature since the elaboration of report D5.3
rationale: Defines the temporal scope of the review.

code_label: Monte Carlo favored for multidimensional finance
text_span: Monte Carlo techniques are the most commonly used methods in the industry for pricing and VaR. This is due to their ability to handle a variety of setups, good convergence properties in multi-dimensional problems, and simple implementation.
rationale: Gives the rationale for focusing on Monte Carlo-based quantum acceleration.

code_label: PDE methods faster for low dimensions
text_span: These methods offer a faster convergence rate than MC methods for low-dimensional problems.
rationale: States a comparative observation about PDE solvers versus Monte Carlo.

code_label: Quantum finance as alternative modeling line
text_span: a distinct research line aims to create quantum-inspired models of the financial industry, rather than attempting to accelerate classical techniques with quantum tools.
rationale: Identifies a separate research direction beyond acceleration.

code_label: QAMC pipeline components
text_span: The construction of an oracle U which is able to load the path probability distribution. The application of a second unitary V which encodes the payoff of the target contract.
rationale: Describes the common algorithmic structure of QAMC methods.

code_label: Three QAMC application blocks
text_span: The works that have applied QAMC to the problem of pricing and VaR can be categorised in three blocks.
rationale: Provides the organizing framework for the QAMC literature review.

code_label: Path-dependent options gaining interest
text_span: there is an increasing interest in the pricing of path-dependent options.
rationale: Highlights a trend observed across recent QAMC applications.

code_label: Initialization as vector and function loading
text_span: The task is to find the decomposition into a set of quantum gates of a unitary Uv such that: |v⟩= Uv|0⟩
rationale: Defines the core initialization problem reviewed in the section.

code_label: Function loading useful for PDFs and payoffs
text_span: This formulation is particularly useful for financial applications since two of the most common tasks in QAMC are the ones of loading a Probability Distribution Function (PDF) and a payoff function.
rationale: Explains why initialization matters for finance applications.

code_label: Unitary synthesis only for special evolution cases
text_span: the unitary synthesis methods are restricted by the fact that UV is a unitary operator, which limits their applicability to price estimation to a few cases
rationale: States a key applicability constraint of unitary synthesis.

code_label: Initialization should preserve relative phases
text_span: the algorithm should recover the target relative phases in the amplitudes.
rationale: Identifies an important requirement that some methods may violate.

code_label: Noisy hardware favors approximate loading
text_span: loading an approximate initial state yields a lower error than loading the exact one.
rationale: Reports an empirical observation about approximation versus exactness on NISQ devices.

code_label: Variational methods attractive but fragile
text_span: variational algorithms have become a very appealing option. Nonetheless, some of them have the risk of adding arbitrary phases into the amplitudes
rationale: Captures the tradeoff between practicality and correctness in variational loading.

code_label: Amplitude estimation reduces oracle calls
text_span: the same task can be achieved using a lower number of calls to the oracle A by means of a wide range quantum computing techniques grouped under the name of Amplitude Estimation (AE).
rationale: States the main motivation for AE methods.

code_label: AE variants grouped into three lines
text_span: three main lines of research are distinguished: • Parallel algorithms ... • Iterative algorithms ... • Generalized Grover
rationale: Summarizes the taxonomy used for AE methods.

code_label: Parallel methods better for NISQ depth control
text_span: parallel algorithms have, in general, more flexibility to control the depth of the circuit, thus making them more suitable for NISQ devices.
rationale: States the practical advantage of parallel AE on current hardware.

code_label: Noise can erase quadratic speedup
text_span: even in low-strength noise, the quadratic speedup for the exponential schedule is not achievable.
rationale: Reports a key negative result about noisy MLAE performance.

code_label: Linear schedule performs best under noise
text_span: in general, the linear schedule shows the best performance.
rationale: Summarizes a comparative finding across schedules.

code_label: Depth limits stop error improvement
text_span: for a two-qubit circuit and beyond seven applications of the Grover operator, the error obtained with the MLAE algorithm does not decrease further.
rationale: Identifies a depth-related saturation effect in experiments.

code_label: Critical points bias MLAE
text_span: these critical points of order m lead to biased estimators in MLAE, and the error cannot be reduced beyond a certain degree, even in the absence of noise.
rationale: States a theoretical failure mode of MLAE-like methods.

code_label: RandomQAE proposed to mitigate critical points
text_span: the authors propose a new algorithm called Random Quantum Amplitude Estimation (RandomQAE), which combines the results from the Grover operator with the results from a second amplification operator Q(A), thus solving the problem of the critical points.
rationale: Describes the proposed remedy for the critical-point issue.

code_label: RQAE estimates amplitude sign
text_span: aim to estimate √a with a sign, i.e. √aeiϕ with ϕ ∈{0, π}.
rationale: States the distinctive target of the RQAE method.

code_label: Generalized reflections improve Bayesian inference
text_span: their results demonstrate that the ELF likelihood functions combined with a Bayesian inference strategy produces better results compared to the conventional likelihood functions
rationale: Reports the comparative advantage of engineered likelihood functions.

code_label: QSP framework recovers improved IQAE
text_span: they recover an improved version of IQAE and devise two AE estimation algorithms; one which produces an unbiased estimator ˜a and one which controls the maximum depth
rationale: Summarizes the methodological contribution of the QSP-based framework.

code_label: PDE quantum option pricing via imaginary time
text_span: the option price can be obtained from the evolution of an initial quantum state according to an appropriate Hermitian Hamiltionian after a Wick’s imaginary time rotation.
rationale: Describes the core PDE-to-quantum-dynamics mapping.

code_label: Variational simulation used for NISQ encoding and evolution
text_span: the proposed quantum algorithm contains two steps: 1) encoding the initial condition into a quantum state and 2) evolve this state according to the Hamiltonian
rationale: States the two-step structure of the PDE-based quantum algorithm.

code_label: High-dimensional readout loses quantum advantage
text_span: the extraction of the derivative price associated to the spot prices of the asset from the quantum state vector would require to obtain the amplitude of a specific computational basis state
rationale: Identifies the readout bottleneck in the high-dimensional PDE approach.

code_label: Future-time expectation reduces complexity
text_span: This strategy requires the appropriate determination of this future time, the generation of all prices and associated probabilities at that future time
rationale: Describes the workaround proposed to avoid direct amplitude extraction.

code_label: Variational PDE method fits small quantum computers
text_span: the algorithm requires quantum circuits with O(poly(d log(ϵ−1))) few-qubit gates and can be implemented in a small quantum computer.
rationale: States the claimed hardware suitability of the variational PDE method.

code_label: Quantum finance modeling via Schrödinger equation
text_span: a Merton-Shrodinger equation with a Merton Hamiltonian is proposed as a more general framework than the Black-Scholes PDE.
rationale: Captures the alternative modeling proposal in the review.

code_label: Deep hedging extended with quantum reinforcement learning
text_span: quantum reinforcement learning techniques are applied by using orthogonal and compound layers.
rationale: Describes the quantum reinforcement learning approach to hedging.

code_label: Quantum deep hedging limited by qubits and model roughness
text_span: A major limitation comes from the number of qubits, as in the simplest case we need 1 qubit per time step to simulate the evolution of the asset prices.
rationale: States a concrete resource limitation of the deep hedging approach.

code_label: Martingale pricing via quantum linear programming
text_span: the proposed algorithms can extract the martingale risk neutral measure from market variables and estimate the value of the derivative.
rationale: Summarizes the main computational goal of the martingale pricing approach.

code_label: Quantum assets framed with density operators
text_span: the probability measure appearing in classical finance is replaced by a density operator, so that the expected value of quantum assets can be defined.
rationale: Captures the conceptual shift in the quantum assets framework.

code_label: No major breakthroughs reported
text_span: there are no new major breakthroughs since (G´omez et al., 2022).
rationale: States the paper’s overall assessment of the field.

code_label: Most recent work is incremental
text_span: the vast majority of the reviewed documents are a continuation of previous works where the performance is improved up to a constant factor
rationale: Summarizes the authors’ judgment on the nature of recent progress.

code_label: Noise is the main limiting factor
text_span: noise was the main limiting factor found in the experiments.
rationale: Identifies the dominant practical obstacle observed across studies.

code_label: Error correction may erase speedups
text_span: the implementation of such error correcting codes makes quadratic speedups ineffective since the instances where an speedup is realizable are impractically large.
rationale: States a long-term caveat about fault-tolerant overhead.

code_label: Near-term value may be energy reduction
text_span: the improvements that can be devised may come from a relevant decrease in energy consumption and not from a speed-wise improvement.
rationale: Points to a possible future benefit rather than runtime speedup.
